newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Foreigners lift Bucharest mkt, trend may reverse.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners lift Bucharest mkt, trend may reverse.

text.p: Most Bucharest share prices climbed on Monday in a bullish mood among foreign investors, but traders said the trend could reverse following government disclosures of changes in proposed portfolio investment rules.
"Foreigners bought heavily, mostly into the first tier. But they may start retreating tomorrow, after the announced amendments to portfolio proposals," a trader said.
The government said on Monday it was replacing an initially proposed four percent capital gains repatriation tax with a 1.5 percent tax on each portfolio transaction.

Two independent indices, the VAB and the BIG, rose by 3.6 percent and 4.23 percent respectively from the previous session, with the BIG touching a new year high. The BIG first-tier index was 3.65 percent higher at 4,365.88 points.
Volumes on Monday rose to 3.9 million shares from 3.5 million and turnover gained some 2.3 billion lei to 15 billion.

Overall, the average prices of 15 stocks climbed, 10 fell and three were flat. Nine companies had no trade and two were suspended. One second-tier stock, car parts maker Apsa, had a new price set after a share split. Most stocks ended on higher quotes due to deals in late trading.
The first tier took 85 percent of turnover, with five of six listings seeing higher average prices and three closing firmer.

Oltchim chemical plant, which took the bulk of first-tier turnover, or 5.2 billion lei, closed 150 lei stronger at 3,250. Pharmaceuticals Antibiotice gained 200 lei to end at 5,400 and Arctic refrigerator maker closed at 3,900, 450 lei higher on the previous quote.
Fertiliser maker Azomures shed 50 lei to end at 3,700 and Terapia pharmaceuticals company ended 350 lei weaker at 6,150.
Sofert fertiliser maker had a weaker average price and lost 2,000 lei to close at 63,000.
Policolor dye maker dominated the second tier, with 1.8 billion lei in turnover. It closed flat at 5,700.
